scenes.headline: How EAGLE-3 teaches a draft model to scale
scenes.sub: Speculative decoding, and the training trick that lets more data help.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Aspen! EAGLE-3 makes a language model up to six and a half times faster, with identical output. Here's how its draft works.

scenes.text: Train the draft the way it runs: predict tokens directly, feed it its own guesses during training, and it keeps improving with more data.

scenes.title: Speculative decoding, the base trick
scenes.say: First, the trick it builds on.

items.text: A small draft guesses a few tokens
The big target checks them all

steps.say: EAGLE-3's draft reads the target's features from low, middle and high layers, not just the top one, and fuses them.
It adds the embedding of the token just sampled, and runs a single decoder layer.
Out comes the next token, predicted directly. No more predicting the target's features first.

steps.note: later steps use the draft's own outputs
steps.say: For the guesses after that, the target's features don't exist yet, so the draft feeds on its own outputs.

left.title: EAGLE
items: Second guess collapses; more data barely helps
left.say: EAGLE trained its draft one step at a time. At step two it fed on its own drifting output, and the second guess collapsed.

right.title: EAGLE-3, Training-Time Test
items: Trained on its own multi-step rollout
Speedup keeps rising with more data
right.say: EAGLE-3 folds that rollout into training, so the draft learns to consume its own predictions. Now the speedup keeps climbing with more data.

scenes.title: Mean speedup over vanilla decoding, Vicuna-13B
scenes.say: Averaged over five tasks, EAGLE-3 runs five point five one times faster than plain decoding, ahead of EAGLE-2 at four point two two.

scenes.text: Acceptance is a data problem: once the draft trains the way it runs, more data keeps buying speed.

recap: A cheap draft guesses; the target verifies
The draft fuses low, mid and high features
Training-Time Test lets speedup scale with data
scenes.say: To recap: guess and verify, a draft fusing three layers of features, trained on its own guesses.
